headline: Critical pre-authentication flaws in BeyondTrust remote-access software and a hidden backdoor in Tenda routers hand attackers control, while China-linked crews mine university webmail and build relay networks.

emerging_trends.text: Critical pre-authentication flaws in BeyondTrust's remote-access software and a hidden backdoor in Tenda routers show attackers keep finding ways to slip past the login screens guarding trusted infrastructure.

China-aligned crews keep quietly milking academic webmail through Roundcube flaws and stitching together operational relay networks, extending espionage infrastructure across universities and compromised hosts.
emerging_trends.topic_title: China-Nexus Espionage on Webmail and Relay Networks

emerging_trends.text: As AI agents gain the run of corporate systems, Microsoft's new execution containers and warnings about ungoverned AI access show defenders scrambling to constrain autonomy they already deployed.

topics.title: Constraining Rogue AI Agents
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft launched an early preview of Microsoft Execution Containers on July 7, a policy-driven runtime that enforces developer-defined constraints on AI agents across Windows and Windows Subsystem for Linux, as Elba Security mapped an ungoverned AI attack surface and Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers proposed a 'Cybersecurity AI Scientist.'
topics.summary: Enterprises have connected AI tools and autonomous agents to sensitive systems faster than they can govern the resulting access, from standing OAuth grants to copilots inheriting human permissions. Microsoft's containers let Windows enforce isolation on agents at runtime, one early answer to autonomy already in production.

sources.title: Microsoft wants to keep your AI agents from going rogue
Your company already adopted AI and nobody is governing access
Researchers make the case for a cybersecurity AI scientist

topics.title: BeyondTrust Remote Access Auth Bypass
topics.latest_developments: BeyondTrust on July 7 warned customers to patch two critical authentication-bypass flaws, including pre-authentication CVE-2026-40138 (CVSS 9.2), in its Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access products.
topics.summary: The flaws let unauthenticated attackers bypass authentication and seize control of susceptible devices, a serious exposure given that both products broker privileged access into customer networks. Administrators should apply the fixed builds immediately.

sources.title: BeyondTrust Patches Critical Auth Bypass Flaws in Remote Support and PRA
BeyondTrust warns of critical flaws in remote access software

topics.title: China-Nexus Espionage on Webmail and Relay Networks
topics.latest_developments: A suspected China-aligned cluster exploited patched Roundcube webmail flaw CVE-2024-42009 (CVSS 9.3) against physics and engineering departments at U.S. and Canadian universities to steal credentials, as Cisco Talos reported the actor it tracks as UAT-7810 keeps building operational relay box networks with fresh custom malware.
topics.summary: Chinese state-aligned crews target academic research accounts and assemble proxy relay infrastructure to mask later operations. Universities running Roundcube should confirm they patched CVE-2024-42009 and hunt for credential theft.

sources.title: Suspected China-Aligned Hackers Exploit Roundcube Flaws Against Universities
UAT-7810 continues building ORB networks using new malware

topics.title: Tenda Router Firmware Backdoor
topics.latest_developments: The CERT Coordination Center warned July 7 that several Tenda router firmware versions embed an undocumented authentication backdoor, CVE-2026-11405, that bypasses password verification to grant administrative access to the web management interface.
topics.summary: The hidden backdoor sits in firmware from Chinese network device maker Tenda and hands an attacker full admin control of affected routers. Owners of Tenda gear should isolate the management interface and watch for a vendor firmware fix.

sources.title: CERT/CC Warns of Hidden Admin Backdoor in Tenda Router Firmware

topics.title: Canada's Offensive Cyber Operations
topics.latest_developments: Canada's Communications Security Establishment disclosed July 6 that it ran offensive cyber operations in 2025 against a ransomware-as-a-service gang, an online foreign extremist group, and drug traffickers.
topics.summary: The signals-intelligence agency confirmed it hacked three separate criminal targets last year, a rare public accounting of a Western government using offensive cyber power against organized crime. The disclosure signals a widening willingness to strike back at ransomware crews directly.

sources.title: Canadian spy agency reports hacking three criminal groups in 2025

topics.title: BonkDAO Governance Heist
topics.latest_developments: BonkDAO said July 6 that attackers holding a large stake of BONK cryptocurrency pushed through a malicious governance proposal, voting roughly $20 million in coins into their own wallets.
topics.summary: The theft exploited on-chain voting itself: a holder with enough BONK leverage passed a proposal that transferred coins directly to the attackers. It underscores how decentralized-governance tokens turn concentrated holdings into a drain-the-treasury attack path.

sources.title: Attackers vote themselves $20 million in BONK cryptocurrency

business_politics.title: Iran Strikes Qatari Tanker Near Hormuz
business_politics.latest_developments: Iran's Revolutionary Guard struck the Qatari gas tanker Al Rekayyat off Oman's coast and set it ablaze, widening the Strait of Hormuz attacks that opened a day earlier and pushing oil up more than 1.5 percent.
business_politics.summary: A projectile hit the Al Rekayyat in the Strait of Hormuz early Tuesday, the British military confirmed, the latest strike on commercial shipping in a chokepoint that carries much of the world's seaborne oil; the attacks complicate talks to end the U.S. war with Iran, lifting crude and sending gold lower.

sources.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Fires Missiles at Ships Near Hormuz
Qatari gas tanker hit in Strait of Hormuz
Oil Up 1.5% After Ship Attacks Near Hormuz

business_politics.title: Samsung Selloff Rattles the AI Trade
business_politics.latest_developments: Samsung shares fell 10 percent despite a record quarterly profit, triggering a global selloff in AI-linked chip stocks and dragging South Korea's market toward bear territory.
business_politics.summary: Investors dumped Samsung Electronics, the world's largest memory-chip maker, on fears its heavy AI build-out spending swamps booming chip earnings, pulling U.S. tech futures and Asian semiconductor shares lower Tuesday as doubts about the AI spending war spread across markets.

sources.title: Samsung shares tumble 10% despite record quarterly profit from AI boom
Samsung Expects Another Record Quarter on Robust AI Chip Demand
Korean Stocks Flirt With Bear Territory, Leading Asian Markets Lower

business_politics.title: Bank of England Flags Equity-Market Leverage
business_politics.latest_developments: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee warned Tuesday that rising leverage in equity markets heightens the threat to financial stability, and said it plans to ease bank capital rules to spur lending.
business_politics.summary: In its twice-yearly report the committee said progress toward resolving the U.S.-Iran conflict eased some stability threats while leaving others in place, as the bank separately moved to loosen a capital rule to boost lending and cushion markets in a crisis.

sources.title: BOE Sees Heightened Threat to Financial Stability as Leverage in Equity Markets Rises
Bank of England plans to ease bank capital rule

business.title: Refugee Youth Camp Faces Federal Cuts
business.latest_developments: ARYSE said federal grants for two programs, including its PRYSE Academy summer camp, end October 1 after the U.S. Office of Refugee Resettlement discontinued them indefinitely.
business.summary: The Pittsburgh nonprofit ARYSE, which serves refugee and immigrant youth, draws a quarter of its $1.1 million budget from the government and now works to weather the loss as the Office of Refugee Resettlement pulls key grants.

sources.title: Pittsburgh refugee youth camp works to weather federal funding cuts

business.title: Hey Babe Reopens Renovated Dining Room
business.latest_developments: Hey Babe unveiled a renovated dining area at the Maverick Hotel in East Liberty, nearly a year after opening.
business.summary: Pittsburgh City Paper's food roundup reports Hey Babe, at 120 S. Whitfield St. in East Liberty, finished renovating the throwback-lounge dining room it opened last year inside the Maverick Hotel, part of a briefing that also previews the coming Picklesburgh festival.

sources.title: A Picklesburgh preview, a major supermarket sale, and more Pittsburgh food news

around_town.title: Parkway East Detour Prep Before Closure
around_town.latest_developments: With the shutdown four days off, PennDOT crews are clearing construction material from detour routes and coordinating traffic signals to keep traffic flowing when the Parkway East closes July 10.
around_town.summary: PennDOT will close the Parkway East between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and the Edgewood/Swissvale exit for 25 days starting July 10 to replace the aging Commercial Street Bridge, rerouting a corridor that carries roughly 100,000 vehicles a day through Regent Square and Swissvale streets.

sources.title: PennDOT working to clear traffic obstacles from Parkway East detour routes for upcoming 25-day closure

around_town.title: Mars and Adams Township Merger Heads to Ballot
around_town.latest_developments: Mars Borough Council voted 6-1 Monday to adopt a joint merger agreement with Adams Township, sending the question to voters in both Butler County communities on the November ballot.
around_town.summary: The proposal would fold Mars Borough into Adams Township as one municipality, dropping Mars residents to Adams's 3.75-mill tax rate while keeping mailing addresses unchanged; Adams supervisors already approved the ordinance last month.

sources.title: Mars Borough leaders approve merger ordinance with Adams Township
Proposal to merge Adams Township & Mars Borough will appear on upcoming ballot

around_town.title: Hazmat Spill Closes 62nd Street Bridge
around_town.latest_developments: An overturned truck leaked corrosive liquid onto the 62nd Street Bridge late Monday, closing the span both directions through the Tuesday morning commute.
around_town.summary: The Senator Robert D. Fleming (62nd Street) Bridge, linking Pittsburgh with Sharpsburg and Etna near Route 28, stayed shut as the Cherry City Volunteer Fire Company, Allegheny County Emergency Services, and the city Bureau of Fire spent hours containing the spill.

sources.title: Overturned truck spills hazardous materials on the 62nd Street Bridge
Semi-truck rolls over on bridge in Allegheny County, begins leaking 'corrosive liquid,' sources say

events.title: Union Pacific Big Boy Visits Leetsdale
events.latest_developments: The Union Pacific Big Boy locomotive, on a coast-to-coast tour for America's 250th, will stop in Leetsdale on Saturday, July 11, after a hoax briefly sparked confusion that the visit was canceled.
events.summary: The historic steam locomotive rolls through Western Pennsylvania this weekend as part of the nationwide America250 commemoration, with organizers confirming the Leetsdale stop for Saturday.

sources.title: Big Boy tour is not canceled, will visit Leetsdale on Saturday

around_teams.title: McCarthy's Quarterback Craft and First-Down Passing
around_teams.latest_developments: Two Post-Gazette pieces examine Mike McCarthy's approach to teaching quarterbacks and his reliance on first-down passing as the Steelers sort how Aaron Rodgers, Drew Allar, and Will Howard fit.
around_teams.summary: One analysis shows how heavy first-down passing drives McCarthy's philosophy and the NFL's best offenses; a companion profile casts McCarthy, who never played the position, as a rare quarterback teacher shaping the Steelers' passers.

sources.title: How first-down passing fuels Mike McCarthy's philosophy — and the best offenses in the NFL
The QB whisperer: Mike McCarthy never played the position, but he has a rare gift for teaching it

around_teams.title: Rodgers and the Old-Quarterback Question
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette video asks whether Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers can follow Tom Brady and Peyton Manning as an older Super Bowl winner.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette weighs Rodgers's late-career title odds against the precedents of Brady and Manning, both of whom won championships well past their primes.

sources.title: WATCH: Can the Steelers' Aaron Rodgers follow Tom Brady, Peyton Manning as older Super Bowl winners?

around_teams.title: Skenes Faces His Biggest Week
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles frames the coming week—the All-Star break amid a rough stretch—as the biggest of Paul Skenes's young career.
around_teams.summary: Skenes, the Pirates ace and lone All-Star, heads into the break trying to steady his mechanics after several rough outings, with Hiles laying out the stakes for both the pitcher and a struggling club.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: This is the biggest week of Paul Skenes' young career

team_usa.title: Belgium Ousts the U.S. in the Round of 16
team_usa.latest_developments: Belgium beat the United States 4-1 in Seattle on Monday to reach the quarterfinals, as Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and set up another goal and Christian Pulisic left with a second-half ankle injury.
team_usa.summary: The defeat ended the host nation's World Cup run at the round of 16 once again, its defensive lapses exposed even with reinstated striker Folarin Balogun back in the lineup; the United States last reached a quarterfinal 24 years ago.

sources.title: USMNT's World Cup dream crushed by Belgium
Pulisic forced off injured for USMNT vs. Belgium

team_usa.title: Pochettino Noncommittal on U.S. Future
team_usa.latest_developments: Mauricio Pochettino declined after the Belgium loss to say whether he wants to stay on as U.S. men's coach, urging fans to keep faith.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino, who took over the United States program ahead of the home World Cup, left his future open following the round-of-16 exit in Seattle.

sources.title: Poch mum on U.S. future; tells fans to keep faith

team_usa.title: FIFA and UEFA Trade Blows Over Balogun Reversal
team_usa.latest_developments: FIFA accused UEFA of hypocrisy Tuesday, its disciplinary chair Mohammad Al Kamali arguing that overturning red cards is common, after UEFA said FIFA crossed 'a red line' by lifting Folarin Balogun's suspension.
team_usa.summary: The clash followed FIFA's reinstatement of the U.S. striker's red card before the Belgium match, a decision UEFA called incomprehensible and unjustifiable and that critics tied to a phone call from President Trump.

sources.title: Fifa accuses Uefa of hypocrisy in latest war of words over Folarin Balogun decision
